<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`  _(via conversationId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_
- `content/docs/ai/index.mdx`  _(via conversationId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_
- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via conversationId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_
- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const), performedByAgentId (literal, a string literal in installAuditWriters; a string literal in provenanceMark))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via conversationId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ExecutionContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/plugins/index.mdx`  _(via clientId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via on_behalf_of (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerMetadata), performed_by (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerMetadata))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via agentId (symbol, a field of interface AuditPerformerSource))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1da9f55db0f4028cd6720fae7e80c6574e7dc67` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fee3637eae384c46a3c5a48284202ba94b12a759` — the merge of head `f62fa7ad00016422c95882f00cbe70eb6be421ec` into base `b1da9f55db0f4028cd6720fae7e80c6574e7dc67`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fee3637eae384c46a3c5a48284202ba94b12a759 && git checkout fee3637eae384c46a3c5a48284202ba94b12a759
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b1da9f55db0f4028cd6720fae7e80c6574e7dc67 f62fa7ad00016422c95882f00cbe70eb6be421ec && git checkout -B drift-repro b1da9f55db0f4028cd6720fae7e80c6574e7dc67 && git merge --no-ff f62fa7ad00016422c95882f00cbe70eb6be421ec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1da9f55db0f4028cd6720fae7e80c6574e7dc67
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b1da9f55db0f4028cd6720fae7e80c6574e7dc67` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review: REWORK (1 item, body only; the code, the pins and the spec prose are accepted)** · PR #34679 · card #34556 · area o2-B · L1-a2 · 2026-11-17T07:31Z

Head-sha: `5f005fb26aac627794032316688a28427b8e2822`

Final-head comment 6941684507; dev report 6940367044; claim amendment 6940394255.

### Checked, no problem

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #34556` is the only closing keyword in the body. It is right: all four enumeration boxes are delivered, and each row kind is pinned. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold. The spec change is describe and JSDoc text only, and no key, type, refine or optionality moves.
- **Scope** (`get_files`, 14 paths, +280/−77):
  - three writers and their tests, plus `audit-writers.ts`;
  - two spec files;
  - three regenerated reference pages;
  - `hook-bodies.mdx`;
  - the changeset.
  Commits: `89ffd4b9`, `0c908ab6`, `647bb667`, `49dc838a`, `c5eafdb1` and `19d92fd2`, plus three `main` merges (`41a26f11`, `e7e0373e`, `5f005fb2`). Each merge's `git show --remerge-diff` is empty.
- **Deviation: extracted, not "export helper". Accepted.** #34547 landed the rule inline in `installAuditWriters`, behind a private `provenanceMark(ctx, key)` reader, so there was no helper to export. The card's ask is "the helper #33694 lands, not a second copy". Extracting the rule as one function, `auditPerformerMetadata`, and calling it from all four writers is the only reading that avoids a second copy.
  - I compared the extraction line by line with the removed block. The rule is the same: client else agent, the agent counted as the recorded performer only when there is no client, marks written only beside that agent, each mark only when stamped, `on_behalf_of` = the row's `user_id` ?? `null`, and no performer ⇒ `undefined`.
  - The record-write call passes the four `provenance` marks in the same order.
  - `attributionMark` trims as `provenanceMark` did.
  - The three writers' old `nonEmpty(ctx.performedBy?.clientId)` also trimmed, so client-only rows read the same as before.
  - It is exported from the module, not from `src/index.ts`, so the package surface does not move.
  - The 15 #34547 pins in `agent-dual-attribution.integration.test.ts` are unchanged and green.
- **Wiring reaches production input.** Each writer's event `context` is a `Pick<ExecutionContext, … 'performedBy' …>`. The doors hand the envelope through: `runtime/src/action-invocation-audit.ts:83` (`ExecutionContext | undefined`), `rest/src/data-action-routes.ts:388` and `rest/src/analytics-dataset-query-audit.ts:39`. So `agentId`, `conversationId` and `confirmationId` reach `auditPerformerMetadata` from the same `performedBy` the record-write path copies into `provenance` (`engine-execution-plumbing.ts:158-174`).
- **Pins and ablations.** Three cases per row kind:
  - the AI call records `performed_by`, `on_behalf_of` and both marks, with `user_id` staying the person;
  - CONTROL: a client alone, and a client beside an agent, record the client with no marks;
  - CONTROL: a person's own call carries none of the four keys.
  Ablations (dev report): setting each writer's wiring back to client-only turns that writer's AI pin red (1 failed in each of the three files). Setting `agentIsRecordedPerformer` to `performedBy !== undefined` turns 5 red (the three new CONTROLs and two #34547 record-write pins). All are restored to `blob == HEAD`.
- **Spec prose.** The `performedBy` JSDoc (`:380-386`) and describe (`:431`) now say the three rows "record the performer and the two marks by the same rule". That is true at this head. No "clientId only" text is left in `packages/spec/src`, `content/docs` or `skills/` (`git grep`). The N3 clause ("where both tells apply the mark decides…") appears in the same words in the JSDoc and describe and in `HookContext.provenance.performedByAgentId`. The three regenerated reference pages match the describes.
- **`hook-bodies.mdx`.** The three added rows match `body-runner.ts:1504-1508`, which copies the four `performedBy*` marks, and the `HookContext.provenance` describes.
- **Changeset** (root `.changeset/`; `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/spec`, both patch). I checked each sentence against the diff, including "an OAuth client stays the recorded performer, also when an envelope names both, and its rows never carry the two marks" and "describe text only". They match.
- **Gates.** 119 derived, 119 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (`34556-gates-ran-r2.txt`).
- **CI on this head** (check-runs, `filter=latest`, 72 runs): `success=60`, `skipped=12`, nothing red or pending.

### R1: the `impersonatedBy` leftover needs a `#N` or a reason I can check

Acceptance notes: "The `ctx.provenance` table in `hook-bodies.mdx` still does not list `impersonatedBy`, which the sandbox also copies. Left out to keep the edit small; noted, not filed." I confirmed it at this head:

- `body-runner.ts:1508` copies `impersonatedBy: provenanceRaw?.impersonatedBy` into the body's `ctx.provenance`.
- `HookContext.provenance.impersonatedBy` is described in `hook.zod.ts`.
- `hook-bodies.mdx` has no `impersonatedBy` line at all.

So a hook-body author reading this table cannot learn that an impersonation write is distinguishable. That is a docs defect, and the PR body names it. The rule for an out-of-scope leftover named in a PR body is a `#N` or a reason it is not a defect that a reader can check (precedent: L1-b R1 on #34539 and R3 on #34513). "Noted, not filed" is neither.

Fix, either:

- **(a)** File it as a finding through filing gate ① (docs, `hook-bodies.mdx` `ctx.provenance` table, cite `body-runner.ts:1508`), and name the card in the Acceptance notes; or
- **(b)** Add the one row to the table in this PR. It is the same table and the same kind of row, and it would not move the L2 surface.

Which one is the area's call. If (a), this is a body-only change and I read only the delta. If (b), I read the one new row against `hook.zod.ts`.

### L2 and landing

- **L2 owed at this head:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (published schema `describe`/JSDoc under `packages/spec/src/**`). R1 (a) does not move the L2 surface. R1 (b) is docs only and does not move it either. Keep `needs:contract-review` until a same-shape PASS at the final head is on file.
- **Landing tier.** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34679` reads `NOT governed`, 357 changed lines ≤ 3000. However, the PR touches `packages/spec/src` outside tests, so it is spec surface and goes to the seat as Tier H, and the area does not land it. Once L1 ACCEPT and an L2 PASS are both on file at the same head, the final four steps apply: seat record and 速读, `pm:awaiting-merge`, review request to the approvers, and the round report.

l2-review#4 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP44onN8RMzsPMqjRq

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5f005fb26aac627794032316688a28427b8e2822`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/action-invocation-audit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/data-export-audit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/dataset-query-audit.ts

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #34556 (body and all four comments: triage 6933961648, claim 6939213173, dev report 6940367044, claim amendment 6940394255), PR #34679 (body, file list, the net diff of 14 files against merge-base `fecd2e95`), the four plugin-audit sources and the two spec files whole at this head, records 6936045381 and 6937613475 on PR #34547, and the 72 check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-invocation-audit.ts`, `packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts`, `packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-query-audit.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/package.json`.

- Check-runs: 72, all completed; 60 success, 12 skipped by path filter or opt-in, none failed, none pending. Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (aggregate and shards 1 to 8), Build Core, Build Docs, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard and both Check Changeset runs are success.
- Accept set of `ExecutionContextSchema.performedBy` and `HookContextSchema.provenance`: unchanged. `execution-context.zod.ts` changes one JSDoc paragraph (two sentences) and the `performedBy` describe string; `hook.zod.ts` changes the `performedByAgentId` describe string by one parenthetical. The `z.object` keys, `z.string().optional()` on each, the `requiredOneOf(['clientId', 'agentId'])` refine and its message, and the outer `.optional()` are byte-identical to the merge-base. Right.
- Stored shape of `sys_audit_log`, the change this PR makes: the `action_invocation`, data-export and `dataset_query` rows can now carry, inside the `metadata` JSON text, `performed_by` holding an in-product agent name (on the merge-base it held an OAuth `client_id` or was absent), and beside such an agent `conversation_id` and `confirmation_id`, each only when stamped. On the merge-base an envelope with `performedBy.agentId` and no `clientId` wrote none of these keys on the three rows, so the row read as the person's own call. `on_behalf_of`, `user_id`, `actor`, `tenant_id` and every other metadata key are unchanged. No column, index or enum value is added. Right, and it is what the card asks for.
- Rows that do NOT change: an OAuth client row on the three kinds is byte-identical (the writers' `nonEmpty` and the shared `attributionMark` are the same test, a trimmed non-blank string; key order `performed_by`, `on_behalf_of` is kept); a person's own row still carries none of the four keys; the record-write row is unchanged (see ④). Right.
- Readers of the old shape: a search of the head tree for `performed_by` and `confirmation_id` outside the writers, tests, changelogs and ADR prose finds no code that parses these keys out of `metadata`: no query, view, index, retention rule or export keys on them. `sys-audit-log.object.ts` mentions the pair in a comment only. No reader on main is broken by the widening.
- Public API: `auditPerformerMetadata`, `AuditPerformerSource` and `AuditPerformerMetadata` are exported from the module `audit-writers.ts` only. `src/index.ts` is not in the diff and the package's `exports` map names `.` alone, so nothing new is importable by a consumer. Right.
- Generated pages: the new `performedBy` describe is present once in `kernel/execution-context.mdx` and in all 12 `performedBy` rows of `data/data-engine.mdx`; the new `performedByAgentId` describe once in `data/hook.mdx`. The reference diff is 14 changed lines, 13 carrying "by the same rule" and all 14 carrying "the mark decides". A search of the head for "clientId only" and "record clientId" under `content/`, `packages/spec/src` and `packages/plugins/plugin-audit` returns nothing. Right.

### ② Semver level

Right. Changeset `.changeset/34556-audit-ai-marks-three-rows.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-audit` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch.

- `@objectstack/plugin-audit` patch holds. The package's exported surface does not move. What moves is stored output: additive keys inside an opaque JSON text column, on rows of one producer path, with no reader in the tree keyed on them, repairing rows that mis-stated an AI call as the person's own. PR #34547 shipped the same keys on the record-write row at patch; the same level for the same keys on three more row kinds is consistent.
- `@objectstack/spec` patch holds. Describe and JSDoc text only; no key, type, refine or optionality moves, and the generated pages follow the text.
- Clause-②: `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present and identical in the PR body and the changeset, and both are true: no accept set narrows or widens, and nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- Changeset prose against the head: true. One loose phrase, of no effect: it says metadata carries `conversation_id` "plus", without the "when stamped" the rule applies to it; the spec describe states the condition.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question in dev report 6940367044 (the spec sentence "The action-invocation, data-export and dataset-query rows record clientId only" becomes false with this PR): answered. The seat chose option A in claim amendment 6940394255 and the correction rides this PR. That amendment also lifts the claim's own "No `packages/spec/**` change" line and supersedes the report's "contract_review: not needed", which was written at the earlier head.
- Deviation, `audit-writers.ts`: the claim allowed only exporting an existing helper; the dev extracted the inline rule into `auditPerformerMetadata` because no importable helper existed. Judged in ④ on the tree: the extraction is the same rule with the same outputs, and it gives the card what it asked for ("through the helper, not a second copy"). Accepting the widened file surface is the lane seat's L1 call; nothing in the contract argues against it.
- Deviation, `hook-bodies.mdx` gaining `performedByAgentId` beside the two ids the card names: prose outside this review's scope, the lane seat's. For the record, `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts` copies all four keys into the sandbox, so the three new table rows name keys a hook body does receive.
- Out-of-scope finding with no carrier (dev report: the `ctx.provenance` table in `hook-bodies.mdx` omits `impersonatedBy`, "noted, not filed"): escalated to the seat. It has no card; file one or put it on an existing docs carrier so it is not lost with this PR.
- Observation for the seat, not a finding on this PR: a search of `packages/` at this head finds no non-test producer that sets `performedBy.agentId` (`assemble-execution-context.ts` sets `clientId` only), so in this tree the three rows change only when the in-product AI path named by the cloud#3826 ruling stamps the envelope. The doors hand the writers the request's whole execution context, so the marks arrive once it does. The card's acceptance is the three pin tests, which is what this head delivers.
- Carried from record 6937613475, still a suggestion to the seat: a decision card asking the owner whether every `performed_by` row must stay classifiable for good. The unclassifiable set (rows of a since-deleted OAuth application, and in-product rows with neither mark) now spans four row kinds instead of one.
- The PR is a draft; that is the seat's Tier H step and does not affect this record.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; the writers build one row from the envelope they are handed.

### ④ Design judgment

N3: closed

Record 6937613475 asked for one clause saying which reading wins when both tells apply. The clause is on the head in all three places the reader rule is stated (`performedBy` JSDoc, `performedBy` describe, `performedByAgentId` describe): "where both tells apply the mark decides, and a matching value with no mark is the client unless an agent shares that string". Both halves are true of the code. A row carries `conversation_id` or `confirmation_id` only when `agentIsRecordedPerformer` held, so a marked row names the agent whatever its `performed_by` string equals. A matching value with no mark was written by the client, or by an agent of the same name whose envelope carried neither mark, which is exactly the exception the clause names. The sentence makes no claim for a value matching no existing application; the preceding sentence already covers that case.

`packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts`, each changed sentence against the four writers at this head:

- "The action-invocation, data-export and dataset-query rows record the performer and the two marks by the same rule." True. Each of the three builders now calls `auditPerformerMetadata(ctx.performedBy, userId)` and assigns the result into `metadata`; the record-write writer calls the same function with its four `provenance` marks. Branch by branch, identical on all four:
  - no context, or a context without `performedBy`: the function answers `undefined`, the assign is a no-op, and the row carries none of the four keys (on the three rows `event.context ?? {}` supplies the empty envelope);
  - an OAuth client: `performed_by` is the `clientId`, `on_behalf_of` is the row's own `user_id` value, and neither mark is written, also when the envelope names a conversation or a confirmation;
  - an in-product agent: `performed_by` is the `agentId`, `on_behalf_of` as above, `conversation_id` and `confirmation_id` each only when a non-blank string was stamped;
  - both performers on one envelope: the client is recorded and the agent is dropped with both marks, as the describe's "An envelope carrying both performers is recorded as the client" and the JSDoc's "drops the agent with its two marks" say;
  - a blank or non-string member reads as absent, so a `performedBy` whose members are all blank writes nothing.
- "It does not move `actor`": still true on all four. `user_id` and `actor` are computed from `ctx.userId` as before; no line that sets them is in the diff.
- The sentences kept from PR #34547 ("only when the agent is the recorded performer", "a client row never carries them", the reader rule) now speak for four row kinds through "by the same rule", and each holds for the three new ones because there is one function.

`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`: the one parenthetical in `performedByAgentId` is the N3 clause, judged above. The describe keeps "the record-write audit writer", which is right for a hook key: `HookContext.provenance` exists on record writes only. No "clientId only" sentence stood in this file.

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`: is the extracted rule the rule PR #34547 shipped? Compared statement by statement against the merge-base:

- Inputs: the same four values. The old `provenanceMark(ctx, key)` read `provenance?.[key]` as a trimmed non-blank string; the new call passes `provenance?.performedByClientId` and its three siblings into `attributionMark`, the same test.
- Precedence: `performedByClientId ?? performedByAgentId`, and `agentIsRecordedPerformer = !performedByClientId && performedByAgentId !== undefined`, both moved character for character. The two marks are read behind that gate exactly as before.
- Outputs: `performed_by`, `on_behalf_of: onBehalfOf ?? null` (called with the same `userId` the row's `user_id` takes), then `conversation_id`, then `confirmation_id`, spread into the metadata object at the position the three old spreads held, so the serialized key order is the same.
